question: Not shared. P-709 asks whether a stopwatch-timed stepping test (FSST) separates fallers from non-fallers within neurologist-diagnosed MCI (CDR 0.5; 22 fallers v 24 non-fallers by 12-month self-report; Turkey). P-1013's ROC sample pools 20 healthy adults of mean age 25 with 20 older adults of mean age 79, labelled MCI by MMSE 20-23 plus a recent fall. Its positive class is either BBS < 40 / TUG > 14 s (Section 2.4) or a fall within 3 months, which coincides with MCI group membership because a recent fall was an inclusion criterion (Section 2.5). Its contrast is therefore clinical fall-risk scores, or old fallers against young controls, not fallers against non-fallers within MCI. P-695 (context only) tests 6-month change in gait speed against prospectively recorded falls in MCI and mild AD (Brazil).
metric: AUC in P-709 and P-1013. P-695 reports age-adjusted logistic-regression odds ratios with no AUC, so it does not share a metric with either.

figures.P-695: Change in gait speed for falls in MCI: OR 31.718 (0.192-525.927), p = 0.185. Only recurrent falls in MCI reached significance (Table 4). No AUC.

matched_figure_check: No figure answers the same contrast. Where the numbers can be set side by side, they agree. P-709's 0.825 lies inside P-1013's TUG-criterion intervals, and every P-1013 AUC (0.82-0.94) lies inside P-709's derived interval [0.701, 0.949]. P-709's 0.825 falls just outside two BBS-criterion intervals (ML 0.87-0.99; mean 0.84-0.99), in one direction only. Those rows score sway during the BBS against a BBS cut-off in a sample half made up of 25-year-olds, which is not P-709's question.
performance_validity: The exclusion does not apply. P-709's AUC is 0.825 and P-1013's AUCs reach at most 0.94, with accuracy at most 0.81; P-1013's 0.99 sensitivity is not the exclusion's metric. P-1013's Table 3 is internally inconsistent: in 7 of 8 rows the printed accuracy lies below both sensitivity and specificity.
reason: The papers do not address the same clinical question. P-709 separates fallers within diagnosed MCI, while P-1013's ROC sets clinical fall-risk cut-offs, or old MCI fallers, against a sample half made up of 25-year-old controls, so condition 1 fails. P-695 reports odds ratios rather than AUC, so condition 2 fails for it. Where P-709 and P-1013 can be compared, both instruments discriminate in the same direction and the AUCs overlap, apart from a one-way miss on two BBS-criterion rows that belong to the unmatched contrast, so no difference beyond uncertainty exists on a shared question.
